candidates.source_body_excerpt: Find out the latest events from September 26 from All Across the Arts columnist Steve Cooke Factory International has announced Common Frequency, a new exhibition on the transformative power of music, curated by the 2026 Adidas Originals Creator Network North cohort. Taking place October 3-6 in the vast North Warehouse of Manchester’s Aviva Studios, home of Factory International, Common Frequency, is a free exhibition and event series created by the adidas Originals Creator Network North - a group of 20 young creatives from across the North West. The exhibition traces the influential presence of music in our lives. Over six months, the emerging creatives in the Originals Creator Network North cohort have come together with the support of Factory International and adidas Originals to interrogate the relationship between music, community and identity. Common Frequency is the outcome - bringing together moving images, visual installation, a zine, and two films, which explore experiences of release and resilience through music. These elements are held within an immersive soundscape carrying words and memories recorded by the cohort. On select days, the exhibition transforms into an event space kicking off with an evening of live music and poetry, featuring musicians from Manchester Camerata (October 3) - the UK’s most relentlessly pioneering orchestra, known for constantly innovating and redefining what an orchestra can be. Audiences can also join a hands-on creative workshop (October 4) in the space, exploring music, identity and transformation, and can meet the adidas OCN North cohort (October 6) to hear about their experiences of curating Common Frequency, with a contribution from DJ and Broadcaster Mary Anne Hobbs, and a relaxed networking session.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: A boy has been rushed to hospital with a broken leg after being hit by a car in Heywood . Emergency services were called to reports of a collision involving a car and a child on King Street at around 3.10pm on Thursday (September 24). The driver, a man in his 60s, was arrested at the scene on suspicion of possessing Class A drugs. He remains in custody. Click here to get the biggest stories straight to your inbox in our Daily Newsletter The child was taken to hospital, Greater Manchester Police said. An air ambulance also landed nearby following the crash. A spokesperson for Greater Manchester Police said: "At 3:10pm this afternoon (Thursday 24 November), Officers were called to reports of a collision between and car and a child on King Street in Heywood. "A man in his 60s was arrested at the scene on suspicion of possessing class a drugs. "The child was taken to hospital with a broken leg. "The driver remains in custody." Pictures from the scene show a large emergency services presence on King Street, including police, paramedics, and firefighters. Another picture shows an air ambulance landing in a playing field off Wilton Grove and Cobden Street, not far from the crash. A spokesperson from Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service (GMFRS) said: "Just after 3.15pm on Thursday 24 September, fire crews from Rochdale and Ashton attended a road traffic collision on King Street, Heywood. "Firefighters worked alongside colleagues from North West Ambulance Service and Greater Manchester Police and one casualty has been taken to Manchester Royal Infirmary.Fire crews were on the scene for around 1 hour 15 minutes.”

candidates.source_body_excerpt: The 4th and final new children’s home has now opened as part of Rochdale Borough Council’s £3.4 million investment into the expansion of its residential provision. Welcoming young people for the first time, the new home ‘Diamond’ will support 3 children with complex needs and disabilities who come into care and comes equipped with features like its own dedicated sensory room. The dedicated sensory room at Diamond House. 12 placements are now provided in total across the new quartet of jewel-named homes, with the others named Emerald, Sapphire and Ruby following suggestions from cared for children. This investment stems from a challenging period nationally for local councils, as authorities continue to struggle in locating suitably available placements for children in their care. Through the provision of these new homes, which offer a warm and comforting homestyle environment to those who need it, more children and young people can now remain in the area that they call home, rather than being placed miles out of borough. Councillor Rachel Massey, cabinet member for children's services and education, said: “As the latest jewel in our crown of new homes, I’m delighted to see Diamond open its doors and its homely and friendly feel will make a real difference to the lives of children and young people who need our support.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Pioneering digital autopsies could cut the need for invasive post-mortems by up to 80 per cent, reducing the distress caused to grieving loved ones. The innovative service is being delivered by the Coroner’s Office for Greater Manchester, in partnership with the NHS, specialist post-mortem imaging provider Anubix, and medical imaging provider TIC Health. Working with pathologists, radiologists and mortuary staff at the Northern Care Alliance the coroner’s office will, where appropriate, provide computed tomography (CT) scanning to help inform a person’s cause of death. Teams will use post-mortem imaging to check if a cause of death can be determined without the need for traditional invasive post-mortems, a process that can cause further distress to relatives during the grieving process across Rochdale, Bury, and Oldham. A number of scans a week will be carried out using the new technology, with a long-term ambition of speeding up the service provided for relatives following the loss of a loved one. Cllr Neil Emmott, leader of Rochdale Council, said: “This is a highly sensitive issue that has been carefully handled. “Working in partnership across the health sector, this will help to futureproof the coroner’s service and ensure families and loved ones continue to get the best possible support. “I know from speaking with residents across Heywood, Middleton, Pennines and Rochdale how invasive post-mortems often causes additional anxiety at a time of grief, so this is a timely and welcome new service.”

Families say they have been told replacement facilities will be provided at Rochdale AFC and Rochdale Council's planned Football and Community Wellbeing Hub at Bowlee Playing Fields. But they are campaigning for the new pitch to be created on land next to the original. The Burnside Centre said it understands why people are disappointed to see the pitch decommissioned, but said one of the reasons the decision was made related to concerns about antisocial behaviour. It added: "The pitch, which dates back to the late 1990s, had reached the end of its expected lifespan and required significant investment to remain operational." candidates.source_body_excerpt: Jamie Dale said rehabilitated ex-offenders need to be part of the support process for prison leavers A former prisoner who runs a support network for ex-offenders said government plans to release inmates early would fail to ease prison overcrowding without support from people who had experienced the system themselves. Jamie Dale, 47, from Rochdale, in Greater Manchester, spent more than 11 years in prison for his involvement in organised crime. He now runs the Old Lags Network, which aims to cut reoffending and bridge the gap between prison and the community. He said many prisoners "fall through the cracks" after release. "Most of the people who return quite quickly have not got great family networks," he said. Dale set up the Old Lags Network in September 2025 to provide support to prison leavers Dale said involving ex-offenders in developing solutions would "drastically reduce the amount of people being recalled to prison". "A lot of them can just end up sleeping on the streets," he said.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Will Place, seen here with his mother Beverley, died when he crashed his car after drinking while watching an England match An inquest jury has found that a man died after drink-driving at speeds of more than 70mph before he crashed into a pub in Heywood, Greater Manchester. Will Place, 23, had been drinking in Rochdale after watching the England vs Slovakia match at Euro 2024 and got behind the wheel of his car in the early hours of Monday 1st July 2024. When police in a marked van saw him pass a red light on Manchester Road, they immediately began following him at high speed - but officers called off the pursuit shortly before Mr Place collided into the White Lion pub. The narrative verdict made no mention about the conduct of police officers who had responded to the incident in the moments before the fatal crash. The inquest jury at Rochdale Coroner's Court found that, on the balance of probabilities, alcohol played a contributing factor to Place's decision-making in the moments before he died. In their verdict, the jury also found that his speed was excessive throughout the pursuit and a bend in the road contributed to the instability of the vehicle. A post-mortem examination following the crash found that Place had suffered catastrophic injuries and he was twice the legal limit for drink-driving.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Could walking 70 miles through Rochdale this October actually change someone's life forever? This October, Rochdale residents have a rewarding new reason to lace up their walking boots and step outdoors. The charity Hearing Dogs for Deaf People is inviting the local community to explore the town’s scenic trails, historic landmarks, and hidden gems on foot- all while raising vital funds to transform the lives of deaf people across the region. The autumn initiative, known as the Great British Dog Walk, challenges participants to clock up a total of 70 miles throughout the month. Supported by the charity’s active puppy training hub based right in Rochdale, the campaign encourages walkers of all ages and abilities to discover new corner-of-the-map adventures or simply add extra distance to their favourite everyday routes. Every step taken carries a powerful meaning behind the mileage. The 70-mile target symbolises the average £70,000 lifetime cost to train and support a single, life-changing hearing dog. By turning routine strolls into sponsored miles, local participants will directly help fund the careful breeding, puppy socialisation, and specialised training required to match these remarkable dogs with those who need them most.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Cultural organisations in Rochdale will share in £15 million being spent across Greater Manchester to boost their impact on communities. Greater Manchester Combined Authority has unveiled the funding package for the region’s thriving cultural sector. The investment is part of new Mayor Bev Craig’s wider commitment to restore pride in every postcode and put ‘things to do’ at the heart of towns and will be spread over three years. The extra funding will help organisations such as grassroots music venues, community theatres, and local production companies to help promote wellbeing, community cohesion and good growth by bringing expertise in new areas including youth engagement, disability arts, community music-making, and grassroots cultural participation. Among those to benefit are Rochdale-based Breaking Barriers, a multidisciplinary production company which co-creates work with local communities to amplify unheard voices, which has received an annual award of £40,000. Parvez Qadir, Artistic Director of Breaking Barriers, said: “We’re beyond excited to be recipients of the GMCA Culture Fund 2026-2029. “It’s a real testament of the impact of our work and how it supports communities, young people, and the appetite for cultural interventions across our boroughs. “We’re proud to have been selected amongst so many incredible organisations, and we look forward to creating long lasting impact.”

candidates.source_body_excerpt: The trial of six men accused of the historic sexual abuse of three girls in Rochdale heard that one of the alleged victims has received £89,000 in compensation. Girl B was allegedly exploited in the mid 2000s. Girl A was said to have been abused in the same period. While the alleged abuse of another, Girl C, allegedly began in the late 1980s. The trio were ‘groomed', 'manipulated' and became 'sex slaves', often being forced to have sex ‘with multiple men on the same day, in filthy flats and houses’, prosecutors allege. Click here to hear the latest from Manchester's courts in our newsletter Tahir Rashid, 55; Mohammed Saleem, 47; Sucklane Shah, 47; Amjad Mahmood, 54; Iftaq Hussain, 46; and Arshad Mohammed, 56, deny all the charges they face. As the trial at Minshull Street Crown Court continued, Girl B was cross-examined in court by Mr Rashid’s barrister, Ayaz Qazi KC. Mr Qazi claimed that Girl B had given ‘limited details’ about Mr Rashid. He put it to her: “I’m going to suggest that the reason you are able to give very limited details about [Mr Rashid] is because they are details you have picked up from [Girl A].” Girl B replied: “No, because if she remembered more she would have told me more, if I was making it up I could have said more. I’m only saying what I remember.” Jurors heard that Girl A and Girl B lost touch but began messaging each other again as adults. Mr Qazi referenced messages from Girl A which mentioned compensation. Asked whether she had received compensation, Girl B said: “I got £20,000 which was from social services, and then I got £69,000 from the CICA [Criminal Injuries Compensation Authority].” Asked for the total figure she received, Girl B said: “It would have been £89.000.” Girl B claims she was raped by Mr Rashid at his home in Rochdale. Mr Qazi put it to her: “You didn’t visit that Bamford house did you?” Girl B replied: “I did.” The KC continued: “And you didn’t engage in any sexual activity with him at that house, did you?” Girl B replied: “I did.” Mr Qazi asked the witness: “Is it your position that apart from that occasion at the VIPER [video identification} parade, you have never had any face to face contact with [Girl A]?" “No, I haven’t," the witness responded. candidates.source_body_excerpt: WHEN the Rochdale women’s team takes to the field for its Northern League 1 fixtures at the Hive, there is an international flavour to the line-up courtesy of an initiative put in place by Hornets General Manager Matt Rigby. Having spent ten years helping develop rugby league in the Netherlands across various roles, including coaching the first national women’s team, Rigby was keen to find a way of benefiting his past and present organisations. “My connection with rugby league in the Netherlands goes back around 10 years, so it is a country and a programme that I have a real personal connection with,” Rigby told Rugby League World. “I spent the last two years involved with the Netherlands Women’s National Team, so I have seen first-hand the potential that exists there. “When you don’t have a domestic competition, it is incredibly difficult for players to develop consistently. For me, bringing players into Rochdale is about giving them an environment where they can play at a good level and experience what it is like to be part of a functioning club programme. For the players, being able to play alongside our women’s team gives them far more exposure to the game than they would otherwise have access to at home. “At the same time, it benefits Rochdale. We get players who are hungry to learn, experience different coaching and bring a different perspective into the group. It is very much a two-way relationship.” Speaking to the Netherlands players, who pay for their own flights to the United Kingdom while Rigby stumps up for their accommodation, the Rochdale experience is as much about a social and cultural exchange as it is about developing their games. “In the Netherlands, we don’t have a rugby league culture, so playing for Rochdale has given me the opportunity to fully experience it,” Vera Van Der Zwan, a physical education teacher from Zwolle and the first Netherlands women’s team captain, explained.
